answer: In an island microgrid, AI agents trade power from turbines on a knoll. Each trading identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before its first bid; a daily market pulse reports which bonds remain locked. An attacker creating 1,000 eligible identities must therefore immobilize $100,000 and bear its financing cost. Generating fresh keys is cheap, but each additional identity requires another bond, limiting how cheaply an attacker can multiply accounts.
